title: Strength Foundations
goal: Learn the main movement patterns
audience: General adult starter template; adapt to saved goals, experience and limitations
progression: Foundation: use a comfortable starting dose, learn technique and record a baseline. Keep 2–3 repetitions in reserve.
Build: repeat the same movements. Add repetitions within the range before adding the smallest practical load; never increase both at once.
Consolidate: retain good technique and comfortable recovery. Reduce volume for fatigue, pain or disrupted sleep; review progress before the next plan.

title: Strength Maintenance
goal: Maintain strength alongside a busy schedule
audience: General adult starter template; adapt to saved goals, experience and limitations
progression: Foundation: use a comfortable starting dose, learn technique and record a baseline. Keep 2–3 repetitions in reserve.
Build: repeat the same movements. Add repetitions within the range before adding the smallest practical load; never increase both at once.
Consolidate: retain good technique and comfortable recovery. Reduce volume for fatigue, pain or disrupted sleep; review progress before the next plan.

title: Run / Walk 5K
goal: Build toward continuous comfortable running
audience: General adult starter template; adapt to saved goals, experience and limitations
progression: Foundation: use a comfortable starting dose, learn technique and record a baseline. Keep 2–3 repetitions in reserve.
Build: repeat the same movements. Add repetitions within the range before adding the smallest practical load; never increase both at once.
Consolidate: retain good technique and comfortable recovery. Reduce volume for fatigue, pain or disrupted sleep; review progress before the next plan.

title: Mobility Foundations
goal: Improve comfortable active range of motion
audience: General adult starter template; adapt to saved goals, experience and limitations
progression: Foundation: use a comfortable starting dose, learn technique and record a baseline. Keep 2–3 repetitions in reserve.
Build: repeat the same movements. Add repetitions within the range before adding the smallest practical load; never increase both at once.
Consolidate: retain good technique and comfortable recovery. Reduce volume for fatigue, pain or disrupted sleep; review progress before the next plan.

title: Recovery Rhythm
goal: Establish gentle movement and recovery habits
audience: General adult starter template; adapt to saved goals, experience and limitations
progression: Foundation: use a comfortable starting dose, learn technique and record a baseline. Keep 2–3 repetitions in reserve.
Build: repeat the same movements. Add repetitions within the range before adding the smallest practical load; never increase both at once.
Consolidate: retain good technique and comfortable recovery. Reduce volume for fatigue, pain or disrupted sleep; review progress before the next plan.

progression: Foundation: use a comfortable starting dose, learn technique and record a baseline. Keep 2–3 repetitions in reserve.
Build: repeat the same movements. Add repetitions within the range before adding the smallest practical load; never increase both at once.
Consolidate: retain good technique and comfortable recovery. Reduce volume for fatigue, pain or disrupted sleep; review progress before the next plan.

title: Nutrition for Muscle Gain
goal: Support resistance training with consistent meals and approved targets
audience: General adult starter template; adapt to saved goals, experience and limitations
progression: Foundation: use a comfortable starting dose, learn technique and record a baseline. Keep 2–3 repetitions in reserve.
Build: repeat the same movements. Add repetitions within the range before adding the smallest practical load; never increase both at once.
Consolidate: retain good technique and comfortable recovery. Reduce volume for fatigue, pain or disrupted sleep; review progress before the next plan.

title: Training Fuel
goal: Practice meals and hydration that support training
audience: General adult starter template; adapt to saved goals, experience and limitations
progression: Foundation: use a comfortable starting dose, learn technique and record a baseline. Keep 2–3 repetitions in reserve.
Build: repeat the same movements. Add repetitions within the range before adding the smallest practical load; never increase both at once.
Consolidate: retain good technique and comfortable recovery. Reduce volume for fatigue, pain or disrupted sleep; review progress before the next plan.
